title: Creole musicians' reading lessons and Joe Snaya
summary: Creole musicians learned to read from teachers; Lewis mentions Joe Snaya, a half cousin of his mother who went north.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: No, I don't, like the styles, maybe I didn't pay attention. But I don't think they were in different styles. I do think they, they were, the Creole musicians, those times, they, uh, everybody went, from Georgia, went to, uh, Old Man Teal, you know, for the lessons they learned to read. Uh, there was another old man, was a Chalini, he was a male, he brought out, all the men he brought out, they were good readers, but they never could, they, they'd no place except in one. And I knew of, anywhere, was, uh, uh, Joe Snaya.

Joe Snaya. Uh, he was a state jungle player. He died some years ago, but, uh, he was a half cousin to my mother in any family. He's older people. And he, he, he left for North, uh, North. And how I saw him, uh, did a while in the U for the first time.
